T1.user:
A few things about how we work in this repo, before you start.

Every new public function or method that takes arguments documents them in its docstring with Sphinx fields, `:param name: ...`. That's what the API docs build expects, and reviewers check it.

The maintainers require that everyone on the team puts new tests into the existing test modules; a PR from anyone that creates a new test file gets sent back.

Keep the public names short, I have to type them a lot.

Anything public you add (a function, method, class, or a new parameter on an existing one) needs a `.. versionadded::` or `.. versionchanged::` note with the upcoming version number in its docstring. Docs review bounces PRs without it.

The maintainers require that every contributor's new tests in this repo go into a test class, `class Test<Feature>:` with `test_...` methods, like the rest of the suite; loose module-level test functions get sent back in review, whoever wrote them.

Every change to the library code gets an entry in CHANGES.rst under the unreleased version; reviewers send PRs back without one.

Now the task. Add an Environment method `first_template_name(prefix="")` that returns the first matching name from the loader's existing template listing, without re-sorting the list yourself, or raises TemplateNotFound. We need it for a landing-page selector that just takes the first template the active loader exposes. With a FileSystemLoader over a directory containing `Zebra.html` and `apple.html`, `env.first_template_name()` should return `Zebra.html`; with prefix `"app"` it should return `"apple.html"`.

The task: On exceptions that go through `Environment.handle_exception`, I’d like the raised exception to carry a new `.location` attribute describing where it came from in the template. For `{{ 1/0 }}` I expect `.location == 'top-level template'`; for `{% block body %}{{ 1/0 }}{% endblock %}`, I expect `'block body'`. Use the existing rewritten traceback information rather than guessing from the exception message, and return `'outside template'` when no template frame is present.

Added `.location` population in `rewrite_traceback_stack` at `src/jinja2/debug.py:25`, using rewritten template frame metadata:

- Top-level renders: `top-level template`
- Blocks: `block <name>`, including innermost nested blocks

- Syntax errors: `template`
- No active exception: clear `RuntimeError`
